analysis: What changed versus the 8 AM PT brief: (1) The tape deepened into midday — S&P 500 -1% and Nasdaq -1.4% near session lows, the Dow slipping into the red, and the Russell -1.4%: still no dip-buy bounce from the CPI repricing, and the selloff is now spreading beyond tech. (2) October hike odds cooled a touch — CME 41.5% vs 43.7-44% at 8 AM — while rate futures imply ~51%, so the two main trackers now disagree by ~10 points; treat any single number as approximate and the read as 'coin flip'. (3) The AI-hardware de-rating broadened from semis to Dell (-10%+, undercutting its 10-week MA), Unity (-9%+) and SMCI (-4%+, five-day losing streak) — capex-hardware is the hot-money exhale trade this morning. (4) NY Fed's Williams gave the market a two-sided read — one more hike this year, none in 2027 — which softens the 2027 path even as October stays live; it partially offsets Bowman's steady-hold signal from earlier. (5) The selloff has a defensive pocket: healthcare and biotech green (Corcept +2%, Ligand higher) while growth bleeds, and the VIX at ~15.7 says the options market is pricing repricing, not panic. (6) Megacap read: Apple +1.2% remains the lone outlier; Meta -3.1% is now the day's worst mega move, consistent with the crowding data (shorts rising in Meta/Tesla). Signal vs noise: CPI numbers and bank prints confirmed across outlets; hike odds vary by tracker so exactness is noise; super-core CPI 2.96% is a secondary-source read (FreedomBunker) — treat with care; Williams/Bowman remarks are official but single-speaker; the CXMT 4F2 claim remains unverified. headlines.headline: Midday tape: the CPI repricing is deepening, not fading — near session lows, S&P 500 -1%, Nasdaq -1.4%, Dow edged into the red, Russell 2000 -1.4%. Still no dip-buy bounce 2.5 hours in.
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is accepting the repricing rather than fading it — the selloff has also broadened from tech to small caps.

headlines.headline: October hike odds: CME FedWatch 41.5% (down from 43.7-44% at 8 AM) while rate futures imply ~51% (Reuters: 49% chance of no change). Trackers disagree by ~10 points — the honest read is coin-flip. Core CPI details: +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected, 2.6% y/y vs 2.5%; super-core 2.96% y/y (secondary source, treat with care). 2Y jumped 13bp to 4.92%, 10Y +9bp to 5.304% right after the print, now 5.24% (+2bp).
headlines.why_it_matters: Odds softened slightly but the tape hasn't — the market is now living with the coin-flip as the base case, and the disagreement between trackers makes any single number approximate.

headlines.headline: NY Fed President Williams said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate once more this year, but sees no need for hikes in 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: Two-sided read: it keeps October live but pushes out the 2027 hiking path — mildly offsetting Bowman's steady-hold signal from earlier this morning.

headlines.headline: Megacap split sharpens: Meta -3.1% to $738.66 (the day's worst mega move), Nvidia -2.7% to $222.41, Tesla -2.4% to $366.04 — Apple +1.2% to $345.31 the lone outlier after its intraday record. The Data Insights September crowding report showed short fund participation rising in Meta and Tesla while long participation rebounded across Mag 7.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rate shocks sell the crowded names first — Meta's sharpest fall lines up with the positioning data showing rising shorts, so this is positioning, not company news.

headlines.headline: AI-hardware de-rating broadens: Dell -10%+ (undercutting its 10-week MA), Unity Software -9%+ (below its 50-day), Super Micro -4%+ on a five-day losing streak (under its 50-day). Memory ETF (DRAM) -3.5%, SOXX -3.5% for a third straight down session.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hot money is exiting AI capex hardware wholesale — ASML's record demand read did nothing for the group, so this is valuation/positioning unwind, not fundamentals.

headlines.headline: Bank wave: Bank of America -6.5% after Q3 profit missed on the $1.2B AML fine, Morgan Stanley -3% despite its beat, BlackRock roughly flat after a +5% premarket peak. S&P 500 Banks index at a 4+ month low.
headlines.why_it_matters: Bank earnings are trading on their merits in a market that has moved on — a rate-fear tape doesn't reward beats.

headlines.headline: Headline September CPI 3.7% y/y (0.6% m/m, largest jump since May) vs 3.6% expected; energy index +5.2%, gasoline +7.1%. Economist Heather Long: the energy shock is spreading — airfares, used cars, recreation, medical and apparel all rose, wiping out 3% wage gains.
headlines.why_it_matters: Breadth of the price pressures is what spooks the Fed — if it were only energy, they could look through it; the spreading services detail is the hike fuel.
